questions.prompt: Which statement distinguishes Node.js from ECMAScript itself?
options: Node.js makes all JavaScript single-threaded in every respect.
Node.js removes the need to handle I/O errors.
Node.js provides host APIs such as filesystem access beyond the language specification.
Node.js defines the browser DOM as part of ECMAScript.
questions.explanation: A runtime adds host capabilities; code should follow those APIs and handle their failures.

questions.prompt: What helps keep module dependencies understandable?
options: Use explicit imports/exports and keep responsibilities cohesive.
Mutate unrelated global variables from every module.
Hide dependencies in string-based eval calls.
questions.explanation: Explicit module boundaries make dependency relationships easier to reason about and test.

questions.prompt: Where should you verify environment-specific behavior related to Build Tools and Bundlers?
options: Only the output from one computer.
A random post that does not identify the runtime version.
The official documentation for the browser API or Node.js runtime involved, alongside the ECMAScript reference for language semantics.
questions.explanation: The specification defines language semantics; host documentation defines environment APIs and compatibility.
